key_insight: Submesoscale frontogenesis can drive strong diapycnal tracer transport, and a large share of the vertical exchange comes from mean advective motion tied to the evolving secondary circulation, not just direct turbulence.
engineering_relevance: Ocean and climate models need to represent this mixed advective-turbulent pathway to better predict vertical transport of pollutants, nutrients, and other tracers across density layers.
method: Large-eddy simulation of passive tracer transport in submesoscale frontal zones
Analyze turbulent fluxes and mean diapycnal velocity during frontogenesis
Separate direct turbulent covariance from mean advective diapycnal transport
evidence_signal: The abstract reports LES results showing intense turbulence during frontogenesis and substantial diapycnal tracer flux into the ocean interior, with both turbulent and mean-advective contributions quantified qualitatively.
watch_item: The mechanism is demonstrated in simulation, so its strength and generality in real ocean fronts may depend on unresolved parameterizations and observational validation.
paper_title: Diapycnal material transport driven by submesoscale frontogenesis
